items.title: Goldman Sachs, SocGen buy Rs 920 crore stake in Lenskart
items.description: Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale have jointly invested ₹920 crore to purchase a 1% stake in Lenskart Solutions, acquiring 65.21 lakh and 61.76 lakh shares priced at ₹725 each. Steadview Capital Management facilitated this by selling an equivalent number of shares, resulting in their stake decreasing from 3.31% to 2.58%. Following this, Lenskart’s stock slid approximately 4%, ending the day at ₹715.90.

items.title: Stocks in news: Adani Enterprises, Tata Steel, PhysicsWallah, Hyundai Motor India, Lenskart and Hindalco
items.description: Indian equity markets experienced a decline as benchmarks reversed early gains due to profit booking. The Nifty 50 index fell significantly, indicating investor sentiment was shifting. Several companies announced developments affecting their stock performance, including Adani Enterprises and Tata Steel. Hyundai Motor India also revealed a price increase due to rising input costs across its vehicle range. Various other companies have made strategic moves, which may impact their future performance.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian equities have felt the heat from last week's international sell-off, with significant fallout in both the banking and commodities sectors. Experts foresee that while global equity weaknesses may spill over into the Indian market, the repercussions will be limited. Current support levels sit at 25,000-25,100 and resistance is registered at 25,500-25,600. Foreign portfolio investors have been active, buying equities worth Rs 5,672.

items.title: Indian markets face fresh volatility test after sharp rebound: Kotak Institutional Equities
items.description: Indian equities are likely to see increased volatility as domestic rallies occur alongside global market sell-offs. Concerns about the impact of global weakness on Indian markets remain present due to negative investor sentiment. Both foreign portfolio and mutual fund inflows have been positive, although insurance company flows have declined. Corporate earnings and crude oil prices are anticipated to influence the market movements in the near term.

items.title: Stock Radar: L&T stock breaks out from multi-month descending resistance trendline; time to buy?
items.description: Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T) stock has witnessed a breakout from its descending resistance trendline, signaling potential growth ahead. The stock has recorded more than a 13% increase this past month, following a robust base around the 3,600 mark. It's advisable for traders to consider buying, aiming for targets between Rs 4,400 and Rs 4,450 in the near future, with a stop loss strategy advised below Rs 4,050.

items.title: NBFCs tap AI to spot defaults early, lower credit costs
items.description: Non-banking financial companies are increasingly adopting AI technologies to enhance their underwriting processes and credit monitoring. L&T Finance reported significant reductions in EMI bounce rates in various portfolios after implementing AI-powered solutions. Poonawalla Fincorp noted improvements in early delinquencies and credit costs as a result of advanced risk decisioning. Kissht also experienced a decline in delinquency rates, demonstrating the effectiveness of these AI initiatives.

items.title: HDFC Bank, Kotak, Axis need faster retail deposit growth for share re-rating: Jefferies
items.description: Retail deposit growth is not keeping pace for HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and Axis Bank when benchmarked against rivals. As per Jefferies, a push for faster deposit growth is crucial for these banks to align with projected earnings. If this trend remains stagnant, they may resort to high-cost funding strategies, negatively impacting net interest margins. Meanwhile, ICICI Bank and SBI thrive in deposits, along with faster-growing smaller private banks.

items.title: Irdai sets up panels to standardise health insurance claim rejections, enable real-time tracking
items.description: To bolster transparency within health insurance claims, Irdai has formed two specialized groups tasked with standardizing rejection reasons. Their objectives include developing consistent reporting standards and introducing a live tracking system for policyholders. The first group's focus is on analyzing claims performance metrics, including turnaround times, while the second will advise on a pilot project for timely claim status updates, with reports expected by December 26.

items.title: Blackstone brings in former HDFC Ergo CEO Ritesh Kumar for India insurance venture
items.description: Underscoring its commitment to the Indian insurance landscape, Blackstone has designated Ritesh Kumar as a 10% shareholder in its emerging general insurance initiative. Targeting the expansive non-life insurance market that surpasses ₹3 lakh crore, the venture is set to leverage advanced technology for AI-driven processes. An initial funding of ₹150-200 crore is earmarked for kickoff, while it awaits green lighting from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India.

items.title: Banks flag NBFC autopay risks amid rising cyberfraud cases
items.description: Rising cybersecurity issues are prompting banks to scrutinize the pre-authorisation practices of non-banking finance companies, which permit unmonitored financial transactions. In light of this, banks are urging for more stringent oversight to reinforce automated payment systems. The Reserve Bank of India is actively engaging with financial institutions and technology firms to tackle these vulnerabilities, highlighting the necessity of periodic assessments of NBFC infrastructures to uphold security against potential fraud.

items.title: OMC stocks to buy: Jefferies favours BPCL, IOCL over HPCL amid falling crude prices, improving margins
items.description: Jefferies prefers BPCL and IOCL over HPCL as falling crude oil prices improve oil marketing companies' profitability outlook. The brokerage sees upside potential of 24% in BPCL and 20% in IOCL, citing attractive valuations, stronger marketing margins and resilient refining spreads, while maintaining an Underperform rating on HPCL.

items.title: Nifty could hit 31,735 in bull-case scenario, says PL Capital. HUL, Astral among top picks
items.description: Indian equities could deliver double-digit returns over the next 12-15 months, according to PL Capital, which has raised its Nifty target to 28,561 in the base case. The brokerage cites attractive valuations, resilient demand and improving geopolitical prospects.

items.title: APL Apollo Tubes among 4 Nifty500 stocks closing below VWAP
items.description: On November 23, four stocks from the Nifty500 universe closed more than 2% below their respective Volume Weighted Average Prices (VWAPs), according to StockEdge's technical scan. VWAP measures a stock's volume-weighted average traded price during the session. A close below VWAP indicates the stock ended the session below its volume-weighted average traded price, signalling intraday weakness.

items.title: Jupiter Wagons shares hit 20% upper circuit after entering JV with South Korea’s Woojin
items.description: Jupiter Wagons shares surged 20% to hit the upper circuit after announcing a joint venture with South Korea’s Woojin Industrial Systems to manufacture metro coaches and propulsion systems in India, including technology transfer for Vande Bharat trains.

items.title: TCS, Infosys, Wipro, other IT stocks gain up to 5%. What’s driving the rally?
items.description: TCS, Infosys, Wipro and other IT stocks rose on Wednesday as investors reassessed concerns over massive AI investments and their potential returns. However, global brokerage Jefferies remains cautious on the sector, flagging weak deal bookings, rising subcontracting costs and competitive pressures despite improving revenue growth and margins.

items.title: HFCL share price hits 5% lower circuit as AI selloff resumes after 1-day breather. More pain ahead?
items.description: HFCL and Sterlite Technologies fell 5% as a renewed global AI stock selloff revived concerns over data centre investments and their returns. HFCL, a multibagger in 2026, has declined 30% in a month.

items.title: NSE shares rise 2% as ICICI Securities gives Rs 2,650 target price while initiating coverage
items.description: NSE shares rose on Wednesday after ICICI Securities initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a Rs 2,650 target price, implying 20% upside from its reference price. The brokerage expects profits to grow to Rs 16,400 crore by FY29, citing NSE's market dominance, rising trading activity and new growth opportunities.

items.title: SG Mart shares hit 20% lower circuit after reaching all-time high; here’s what happened
items.description: SG Mart shares plunged, extending losses after hitting a record high in the previous session, as investors booked profits. The stock had surged 15% on Monday following the company's announcement that its board would meet on November 26 to consider a fundraise.

items.title: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank shares trade at a discount to global peers despite rally: Jefferies
items.description: Indian financial stocks have underperformed global peers since 2024, but their valuations have turned attractive. Jefferies sees scope for further gains, with stronger earnings growth and revised price targets for HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank.

items.title: Tata Steel shares fall 12% in 3 days, but Jefferies, Motilal Oswal remain bullish. Should you buy the dip?
items.description: Tata Steel shares have fallen 12% in three sessions following the company's proposed acquisition of a controlling stake in APL Apollo Tubes. However, Jefferies and Motilal Oswal remain bullish, citing the strategic benefits of expanding downstream operations, attractive valuations and potential margin gains. Both brokerages retain Buy ratings.

items.title: PB Fintech, Turtlemint shares jump 5%: What changed and what Jefferies sees ahead
items.description: PB Fintech and Turtlemint shares rose on Wednesday after IRDAI set up a committee to review proposed changes to insurance distribution commissions. Jefferies sees potential upside for PB Fintech if commission rules are relaxed, projecting up to 40% higher FY30 profit after tax under a favourable regulatory scenario.

items.title: Hyundai Motor India shares fall over 2% as carmaker hikes prices across select models
items.description: Hyundai Motor India has decided to raise prices on select car models due to rising costs. The price hike is limited to Rs 8,000 and varies by model and variant. This marks the fourth price increase this year following earlier hikes in January, June, and September. Major automakers like Maruti Suzuki and Tata Motors have also announced similar price increases to manage costs.

items.title: Why did market rally today? Sensex soars 1,502 pts, Nifty ends above 25,800; 5 key factors fuelling bull run
items.description: On Wednesday, benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty experienced a substantial rebound, fueled by widespread buying interest. Following a striking sell-off earlier in the week, both indices collectively recovered around Rs 3.5 lakh crore in market capitalization. Major contributors to this uplift were large-cap stocks like HDFC Bank and Reliance Industries.

items.title: APL Apollo Tubes shares: Buy on dips or wait for a reversal after Monday's rout? Here's what charts suggest
items.description: APL Apollo Tubes saw a significant drop of over 21% after the announcement of a deal with Tata Steel, triggering alarm among investors about the stock's viability. Analysts suggest refraining from aggressive buying during the dip until a recovery pattern emerges. With support levels hovering between Rs 1,580 and Rs 1,600, further declines are on the horizon. Buyers should wait for more clarity before proceeding with any investments.

items.title: A Rs 43,000 crore bet on banks and financial stocks: What changed in FIIs’ November flows?
items.description: In November, Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) directed their attention to banks and financial stocks, pouring in Rs 43,102 crore in just the first half of the month. Telecom, automotive, and consumer services sectors also attracted significant funding. However, despite this robust influx, valuation concerns regarding market prices linger, resulting in a discerning investment strategy across multiple sectors.

items.title: Physicswallah shares in focus as firm enters higher education with digital university in Punjab
items.description: Physicswallah is entering the higher education space with the launch of Physicswallah Digital University in Patiala, following the Punjab government's notification of the enabling Act. The university is expected to begin its first academic session in July 2027. The move expands the edtech company's presence beyond its existing education offerings.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Thursday
items.description: Sensex surged 1,502 points and Nifty gained 470 points on Wednesday, recovering from Monday's sell-off. Banking, FMCG and IT stocks led broad-based buying, adding nearly Rs 3.5 lakh crore to BSE-listed companies' combined market capitalisation.

items.title: GIFT Nifty futures fall 0.53% after US tariff proposals on India; Wall Street slides, Nasdaq drops 4%
items.description: GIFT Nifty fell 138.50 points amid fresh US tariff proposals targeting India and 13 other economies. The proposed duties of up to 25% on Indian goods triggered caution despite a strong domestic market rally, while Wall Street slumped.

items.title: Carlyle pares 7.4% stake in Piramal Pharma for over Rs 2,211 crore
items.description: The Carlyle Group has divested 7.4 percent of its stake in Piramal Pharma through an open market deal, selling approximately 9.86 crore shares at an average rate of Rs 224.17 each. As a result, its stake decreased from 17.93 percent to 10.52 percent. Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund was the most significant buyer, acquiring over 2.12 crore shares. Subsequently, Piramal Pharma's share price dropped by 1.

items.title: Opening a demat account to get easier as Sebi simplifies a host of KYC rules. Check details
items.description: SEBI has revised its KYC framework to simplify demat and trading account opening, reduce repetitive documentation and improve KYC portability. Effective December 24, 2026, the changes centralise investor information, ease verification and streamline address and name updates.

items.title: Sebi retains BSE 200, Nifty CPSE on key indices list despite failing Rs 20,000 crore AUM test
items.description: SEBI has retained BSE 200 and Nifty CPSE in its significant indices list despite both failing the Rs 20,000 crore AUM threshold during the January-June 2026 review. The regulator's latest decision leaves the existing list unchanged.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: An aviation major for a 6% rise, a large-cap FMCG stock for a 7% gain
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: SEBI eases KYC norms, centralises supplementary client data to simplify onboarding
items.description: SEBI has revealed new measures aimed at simplifying the client onboarding process for investors. By centralising supplementary KYC details with KYC Registration Agencies, investors can avoid repetition. The revised framework will take effect on December 24, 2026, enhancing efficiency in data management. Intermediaries are instructed to report account closures promptly to maintain accurate KYC records. Investors are also advised against engaging with grey market premium figures for IPOs.

items.title: Sebi mulls early payout of up to 80% of sale proceeds to FPOs in commodity derivatives market
items.description: Sebi introduced a proposal for an early pay-out framework designed to assist Farmer Producer Organisations. This framework would allow FPOs to access up to 80 percent of sale proceeds before contract expiry. The initiative aims to alleviate liquidity challenges by providing timely payments to farmers. Corporate trading members will offer this facility based on certain conditions and net worth requirements. Public comments on the proposal are invited until December 16.

items.title: RBI may opt for 25 bps rate hike as oil eases, inflation risks persist: Baroda BNP Paribas MF CIO
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India is projected to implement a 0.25 percent interest rate hike in December. While decreasing crude oil prices could alleviate some inflation worries, many senior executives advocate for a measured strategy due to the prevailing economic climate. Nevertheless, concerns regarding food inflation and supply chain issues persist, adversely influencing overall forecasts.

items.title: Mood decides prices for a season. Policy decides the structure for a decade: 5 stocks from the water management space
items.description: When it comes to structural change in a sector, it has nothing to do with the market. It does not stop because the market is facing strong headwinds, as it was a month ago; nor will it gather strength because those headwinds have eased. Such change happens to its own logic, and in the water management space that logic is policy and need, not the market’s mood today.

items.title: Market wrap: HUL, Tata Consumer, Tata Steel, Max Healthcare top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Wednesday
items.description: Indian stock markets staged a strong rebound on Wednesday, with the Sensex surging 1,502 points and the Nifty gaining 470 points to reclaim the 25,800 mark. HUL led the gainers on both indices, while Tata Steel topped the losers' list. FMCG and financial stocks powered the rally.

items.title: Shapoor Mistry lobbied Modi twice for Tata Sons IPO as battle over listing intensifies
items.description: Shapoor Mistry, the head of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, has reached out to Prime Minister Modi regarding the listing troubles faced by Tata Sons. He claims that Tata Trusts are obstructing the public offering for their own benefit and breaching regulations. Meanwhile, the Reserve Bank of India has pressured Tata Sons to meet listing necessities.
